# pidginhost_bucket_credentials (Resource)

The S3 access key and secret key of a bucket. Creating this resource reads the keys the bucket already has, so clients that use them keep working. Changing rotation_triggers rotates the keys. Replacing the resource, for example for a new bucket_id, reads the keys again without rotating them. Terraform reads the keys only when it creates or rotates them, never on refresh, since the API records every read and rotation in an audit trail. Destroying the resource only removes the keys from the Terraform state: they stay valid.

## Example Usage

```terraform
resource "pidginhost_bucket" "media" {
  name     = "media"
  quota_gb = 10
}

# Reads the bucket's current keys. Changing rotation_triggers rotates them.
resource "pidginhost_bucket_credentials" "media" {
  bucket_id = pidginhost_bucket.media.id

  rotation_triggers = {
    rotated = "2026-10"
  }
}

output "media_secret_key" {
  value     = pidginhost_bucket_credentials.media.secret_key
  sensitive = true
}
```

<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
## Schema

### Required

- `bucket_id` (String) Id of the bucket. Changing it replaces the resource and reads the keys of the new bucket.

### Optional

- `rotation_triggers` (Map of String) Arbitrary values, for example a date. Any change to this map, including setting it for the first time, rotates the keys in place: the API issues a new pair and revokes the old one, so clients still using the old keys stop working.

### Read-Only

- `access_key` (String, Sensitive) S3 access key.
- `id` (String) Identifier of the object in the PidginHost API.
- `secret_key` (String, Sensitive) S3 secret key.
